newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico subsidizes wheat sales by 150 mln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Mexico subsidizes wheat sales by 150 mln pesos.

text.p: Mexico subsidizes its internal wheat sales by 150 million pesos, Jalisco state Rural Development Minister Francisco Mayorga Castaneda said.

The federal government recently said "it will give aid of 150 million pesos to alleviate a little the fall in prices and avoid wheat sale difficulties," Mayorga said in an interview with Reuters on Thursday.

Farmers receive 1,423 pesos per tonne of wheat, of which 100 to 120 pesos come from the federal government in financial and storage aid. Mexican millers pay about 1,570 pesos for imported wheat, he said.
"(The program) will be unequal because it will not cover all wheat producers," he added, saying the funds will only reach about half of growers.

Wheat millers are against the subsidy program because of the administrative red tape to get the financial aid, and because growers have already sold most of the crop, he said. Growers have threatened to seize warehouses or block roads if their complaints are not settled, Mayorga added.
He said most of the largest wheat producing states have completed more than 80 percent of the wheat harvest.
"There is still wheat left over from last harvest and this has kept demand weak from buyers, and the international market has been down compared with last year," he said.
Jalico's Rural Development Ministry estimates 1997 national wheat output of 3.05 million tonnes, compared with 4.15 million tonnes harvested in 1994.
